question.text: A metal is heated in a furnace where a sensor is kept above the metal surface to read the power radiated (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>) by the metal. The sensor has a scale that displays <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mfrac><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></mfenced><mi> </mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is a constant. When the metal surface is at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>487</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the sensor shows a value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>. Assume that the emissivity of the metallic surface remains constant. What is the value displayed by the sensor when the temperature of the metal surface is raised to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2767</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>?
